import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V, mask=None):
    d_k = Q.size(-1)
    scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / (d_k ** 0.5)
    if mask is not None:
        scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
    weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
    return torch.matmul(weights, V), weights

diagram_caption: Self-attention matrix computation flow from input embeddings to context vectors.

content.tldr: The Transformer discards recurrent processing in favor of parallel self-attention, allowing tokens across an entire sequence to dynamically compute pairwise relevance scores simultaneously.
content.simple_explanation: Rather than passing an internal hidden state sequentially like an RNN, the Transformer projects input embeddings into Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V) matrices. Each token Query calculates a dot product with all token Keys, divided by the square root of the key dimension to prevent gradient saturation. A softmax function normalizes these products into attention weights, which scale the Value vectors to construct contextual representations in parallel.
content.real_world_example: Think of a database lookup system where each word submits a search request (Query), matches against metadata tags of all available documents (Keys), and retrieves weighted content (Values) proportionally to relevance.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: While attention eliminates sequential recurrence bottlenecks during training, computing all token pairs creates quadratic time and memory complexity O(N^2). Without causal masking in decoder autoregression, tokens would cheat during generation by attending to future ungenerated positions.
